title: Alembic Migrations Handbook
summary: Quick revision notes on Alembic for SQLAlchemy projects: setup and env.py wiring, the autogenerate workflow and its blind spots, upgrade/downgrade commands, async engine configuration, and safe deployment of migrations.

chapters.title: Alembic Mental Model and Setup
points: Alembic is the migration tool for SQLAlchemy: a linear (or branched) chain of revision scripts, each with revision and down_revision identifiers
The current DB state is stored in the alembic_version table, which holds the single head revision ID that has been applied
alembic init alembic creates alembic.ini, an alembic/ folder with env.py, script.py.mako and versions/; use 'alembic init -t async alembic' for the async template
Set sqlalchemy.url in alembic.ini or override it in env.py from app settings (e.g. config.set_main_option); never commit real credentials in alembic.ini
Alembic vs create_all(): create_all only creates missing tables and never alters or tracks versions, so it is not a migration tool

chapters.title: env.py and target_metadata
points: env.py is the script run on every alembic command; it builds the engine and calls context.configure() then context.run_migrations()
target_metadata = Base.metadata is what autogenerate compares against the live database; the default None means autogenerate finds nothing
Models must be imported (directly or via a package __init__) before env.py reads Base.metadata, or their tables are missing from it
Offline mode (--sql) emits SQL using the URL only with no DB connection; online mode connects and runs migrations in a transaction
Useful configure() flags: compare_type=True to detect column type changes, include_schemas=True for multi-schema, render_as_batch=True for SQLite

chapters.title: Autogenerate Workflow and Its Limits
points: Generate: alembic revision --autogenerate -m "add user email" diffs target_metadata against the DB and writes a script to versions/
Autogenerate detects: added or removed tables and columns, nullable changes, added or removed indexes and unique constraints, and foreign keys
Autogenerate misses: table or column renames (seen as drop plus add and so data loss), most server_default changes, CHECK constraints on some backends, and enum value changes
Always read and edit the generated script before applying; it is a draft and not a guarantee
Data migrations and backfills are never generated: write them by hand with op.execute() or bulk_insert, and split a NOT NULL addition into add nullable, backfill, then set NOT NULL
Use op.alter_column(..., new_column_name=...) by hand for a rename to preserve the data

chapters.title: Upgrade, Downgrade and Naming
points: alembic upgrade head applies all pending revisions; upgrade +1 applies one; upgrade <rev> targets a specific revision (a unique prefix works)
alembic downgrade -1 reverts one step; downgrade base reverts everything; every revision needs a working downgrade() if you want rollbacks
Inspect state with alembic current, alembic history --verbose and alembic heads; alembic stamp head marks the DB as up to date without running anything
Naming: set file_template = %%(year)d_%%(month).2d_%%(day).2d_%%(rev)s_%%(slug)s in alembic.ini for sortable filenames, and write clear -m messages in the imperative
Multiple heads occur when two branches both add a revision: fix with alembic merge heads -m "merge" and never edit old applied revisions

chapters.title: Async Engines and Deploying Migrations
points: Alembic is synchronous: with an async driver (asyncpg, aiosqlite) env.py builds an async_engine_from_config and runs the migrations through connection.run_sync(do_run_migrations) inside asyncio.run()
Async env.py pattern: do_run_migrations(connection) calls context.configure(connection=connection, target_metadata=target_metadata) then context.run_migrations() inside context.begin_transaction()
The template generated by 'alembic init -t async' provides this env.py, so start from it instead of hand-writing
Deploy order: run alembic upgrade head as a one-off release step or init job before starting the new app version, not inside every app replica's startup, to avoid concurrent runs
Make migrations backward compatible (expand then contract: add the column first, deploy the code, drop later) so old and new code both run during rollout, and take a backup before destructive changes

chapters.title: Alembic Cheat Sheet
points: Setup: alembic init [-t async] alembic, then set sqlalchemy.url and target_metadata = Base.metadata
Create: alembic revision --autogenerate -m "msg"; review the script before applying
Apply: alembic upgrade head | +1 | <rev>; revert: alembic downgrade -1 | base
Inspect: alembic current | history --verbose | heads; fix state with stamp; fix branches with merge heads
Autogenerate misses renames, server_default changes, enum changes and data; handle by hand
Deploy: run upgrade head once as a release step, with expand then contract changes
